input.summary: The original author data are unavailable, so reanalysis is not feasible. This draft proposes a new-measurement descriptive pilot using an emulated network testbed to observe TCP flow completion time under two conditions (no added delay vs. 20 ms added delay) at a fixed bottleneck bandwidth. Because the packet contains no filled design fields, three key decisions remain unresolved and are surfaced as clarification questions. No statistical decision rule or falsification criterion is included; the server will supply descriptive policy.
clarification_questions: What bottleneck bandwidth (in Mbit/s) and queue size should be emulated, and what TCP flow size(s) or duration(s) should be used as the primary input workload?
How many replications per condition are desired for this pilot, and is there a wall-clock or cost budget that bounds the total run time?
Should the delay be applied one-way (sender→receiver) or round-trip, and should any packet loss rate be emulated alongside the 20 ms delay condition?

proposal.problem: The original recorded data from the cited paper are unavailable, making direct reanalysis impossible. An independent new-measurement pilot is the available path to observe the described effect.
proposal.question: Under fixed emulated bottleneck conditions, does adding 20 ms delay produce a measurable difference in TCP flow completion time compared to a no-added-delay baseline?
proposal.hypothesis: Under fixed emulated bottleneck conditions, adding 20 ms delay changes TCP flow completion time.
proposal.conditions: Two conditions: (A) fixed bottleneck, 0 ms added delay; (B) fixed bottleneck, 20 ms added delay. Bottleneck bandwidth, queue size, flow size and delay directionality are unresolved pending owner decisions.
proposal.related_work: The claim originates from a synthetic networking paper citation (sha256: aaaa…aaaa); no full text or prior measurement data are available for comparison.
proposal.alternatives: The observed difference in flow completion time could reflect queuing delay accumulation, retransmission behavior, or slow-start interactions rather than the delay alone; these mechanisms are untested alternatives, not established facts.
proposal.design: A new-measurement emulated pilot using a netem-based testbed, contrasting TCP flow completion time across the two delay conditions at a fixed bottleneck. Replications, flow parameters and resource limits remain unresolved.
proposal.metrics: Primary metric: TCP flow completion time (milliseconds) per flow per condition. Secondary: per-condition range of observed values across replications.
proposal.controls: Bottleneck bandwidth, queue discipline, TCP congestion control variant, flow size and host configuration are held constant across conditions; only the added delay value varies.
proposal.inputs: Emulated network topology with configurable netem delay; TCP traffic generated by iperf or equivalent. Specific flow sizes, bandwidth and queue parameters are unresolved.
proposal.limitations: Source data are unavailable so no reanalysis of original values is possible. Simulation results cannot establish real-world performance or causality. Delay directionality and flow workload are unspecified until owner decisions are recorded.
